title: Remove features constant on fit rows
when: Many constant or all-missing features; no target values are required.
mechanism: Fit the retained column set on fit rows, then use exactly that set for validation/test.
cautions: Do not decide which columns to retain using held-out labels or test variation. This is a complexity reduction, not a promised score gain.

inspected_code_reference.adaptation_notes: The notebook removes constant features, but also contains target-dependent grouping, train/test distribution filtering, local helper imports, file IO, Python-2 syntax and 100 repeated model fits. Those parts are not copied into the runtime example. Supervised grouping would need fit-only/OOF handling. Original notebook is linked, not bundled or advertised as runnable Python 3.12.

title: Preserve missingness before imputation
when: Missing features and an owned median-imputation base without indicators.
mechanism: Add row-wise missing flags before the fitted imputer. Select columns using fit rows only.
cautions: Native-NaN CatBoost already preserves numeric missingness; median-imputation is not its limitation. Missingness can shift between train and test.

title: Fit-only frequency features for categories
when: Repeated categorical levels where prevalence may convey information.
mechanism: Fit relative-frequency maps on fit rows, add frequencies, map unknown levels to zero, retain original features.
cautions: No target values are used. Frequency can reflect sampling drift; do not learn maps from validation or test.

title: Logarithms for selected nonnegative features
when: Nonnegative counts or skewed magnitudes; inspect distributions before selecting columns.
mechanism: Apply log1p to explicitly selected columns, then fit preprocessing and a suitable linear model.
cautions: This transforms features, not the target. Do not transform arbitrary signed measurements or assume an isolated gain from a blended Kaggle solution.

title: Native categories versus ordinal prefixes
when: Categories with no meaningful order; compare native category models or fitted one-hot representations.
mechanism: Owned CatBoost uses string categories and numeric NaN directly. HGB/tree recipes ordinal-encode categories; linear recipes one-hot encode.
cautions: Never describe all catalogue recipes as median/ordinal. One-hot may be expensive at high cardinality.

title: Rare and unseen category handling
when: Many low-count levels or unseen levels in test features.
mechanism: Fit category vocabularies and optional rare-level grouping on fit rows, preserve an explicit unknown path.
cautions: Do not build a train+validation vocabulary. Do not import the source competition's thresholds unchanged.

title: Choose target transformations under the actual metric
when: Regression with skewed targets or scale-dependent errors.
mechanism: Fit the target transformation on fit labels only and invert predictions before authoritative evaluation.
cautions: RMSE, RMSLE and MAE optimize different errors. Log-target training can bias original-scale predictions. Use current measured comparisons.

title: Candidate interactions from data structure
when: A plausible relationship among features, even if marginal correlations look weak.
mechanism: Propose bounded products, ratios with safe denominators, or domain-motivated combinations jointly with an appropriate model.
cautions: Low pairwise association does not establish independence or absence of useful interactions. Prevent feature explosion and nonfinite values.

title: Learned aggregates respecting split boundaries
when: Repeated entities, groups or sessions with usable group identifiers.
mechanism: Fit feature-only group statistics on fit rows and define an unknown-group fallback.
cautions: Target aggregates require out-of-fold construction inside fit. Entity leakage can make a random holdout misleading.

title: Temporal features with an inference-time boundary
when: Timestamps or repeated measurements with a real temporal prediction setting.
mechanism: Use calendar features and only lags/rolling statistics available at prediction time.
cautions: The mere presence of a year column does not prove a forecasting task. Future observations and labels cannot enter features.

title: Match validation to repeated entities and time
when: Entity reuse, duplicates or chronological drift.
mechanism: Inspect whether the frozen validation reflects deployment. Explain a mismatch explicitly before proposing actions.
cautions: Researchers cannot mutate the frozen protocol. A Kaggle random-fold recipe is not authority for the current split.

title: Multiclass imbalance and decision rules
when: Multiclass labels with unequal representation or poor minority-class recall.
mechanism: Inspect class support and confusion patterns; consider regularization, class weights or training-only sampling under the requested metric.
cautions: Accuracy, macro-F1 and log-loss can disagree. Class weighting changes probability calibration; binary thresholds do not transfer directly.

title: Use error slices to select a next experiment
when: A measured model with errors concentrated in interpretable groups.
mechanism: Connect an error pattern to a feature/model hypothesis and measure the complete proposed solution.
cautions: Group bias alone does not prove underfitting. Repeated use of validation diagnostics can overfit the holdout.

title: Encoded and regularized linear alternatives
when: Sparse categories, additive structure or a cheap complementary model.
mechanism: Fit one-hot categories, scale numeric columns inside fit and tune regularization on the frozen protocol.
cautions: Binary AUC scores from category-encoding competitions are not multiclass performance evidence.

title: Budget-aware boosting capacity search
when: A measured boosting base whose capacity or regularization remains uncertain.
mechanism: Coordinate learning rate, iterations, leaf capacity and regularization using measured durations and scores.
cautions: Iteration counts are not comparable across CatBoost and HGB. A tuning series is optional; preserve time for refit.

title: Blend genuinely complementary predictions
when: Several measured, compatible models with complementary errors and remaining compute.
mechanism: Use predictions aligned to the same protocol; train stacking layers only on out-of-fold base predictions.
cautions: A 33-model, multi-layer winning ensemble is not a three-hour recipe. In-sample stacking leaks labels. No gain is assumed.

title: Keep supervised feature learning inside fit
when: Target encoding, feature selection, target transforms or supervised preprocessing.
mechanism: Fit every learned operation within the returned pipeline. Build training encodings out of fold when they use targets.
cautions: Never use held-out labels or source-competition leaks. A reported leaderboard improvement does not certify honest validation.
